findings.claim: Across the full observed window, landmark_00 soft mass shows a positive whole-window trend (whole_window_z ~ +0.64) with 14 independent batches, but the node-level rate reverses sign (first_rate_z ~ +9.3, last_rate_z ~ -10.0) and the cubic fit is rejected (relative_node_RMSE ~0.29, 4 sign changes, 1 strong sign conflict). This is a non-monotone, batch-dependent contrast rather than a stable directional target.

Landmark_00 local displacement components are dominated by sign reversals and strong sign conflicts: dx (6 sign changes, 9 strong conflicts), dy (6 sign changes, 4 conflicts), dz (10 sign changes, 7 conflicts), cxy (9 sign changes, 14 conflicts). No polynomial is accepted for any of these features, so no stable monotone coordinate direction is supported over the observed support.

Landmark_00 local shape components (cxx, cyy, czz, cxz, cyz) likewise show rejected polynomial fits and multiple sign changes (4-7 each) with strong sign conflicts, indicating the observed coordinate contrast is not a stationary target across the window.

hypotheses.direction: weaker early control vs stronger early control, tested as a contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: No difference in the soft-mass trajectory between early-weighted and late-weighted dose schedules after accounting for total delivered displacement, or the difference is not reproducible across independent batches.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass curve over the observed score nodes [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.scope: whole observed window, all 14 independent batches
hypotheses.statement: If the landmark_00 soft-mass contrast is genuinely time-varying rather than a stationary target, then a dose schedule that shifts guidance weight toward the early portion of the observed score nodes should produce a measurable change in the soft-mass trajectory relative to the uniform-dose reference, while a schedule that only rescales total delivered displacement should not.

hypotheses.direction: unchanged control unless batch-reproducible sign is demonstrated
hypotheses.falsifier: Late-window rate sign flips across independent batches, confirming the reversal is batch-dependent noise rather than a stable temporal signal.
hypotheses.statement: If the landmark_00 local displacement sign reversals reflect genuine within-window turnover rather than noise, then the sign of the late-window rate should be reproducible across independent batches; if it is not, no temporal dose direction is justified for these coordinates.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curve features and trend tables were delivered.
No decoded final affinity or descendant survival labels are present in the role input, so selection preference cannot be distinguished from measured final benefit.
All polynomial fits for landmark_00 features are rejected (polynomial_accepted=false), so no extrapolation beyond the observed support is supported.
The observed coordinate features are untyped proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
The registered dose recipes (W1/W2/W3) are proposed interventions, not parameters learned from the observed temporal slopes.
